Use the quadratic formula: x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac)) / (2a). Calculate the discriminant (b² - 4ac) to determine the number of real solutions. Plug the values into the formula and simplify. This will give you the roots of the equation.

To find stationary points, take the first derivative of the function, f'(x). Set f'(x) = 0 and solve for x. These x-values are the points where the slope is zero. Plug each x-value back into the original function to find the corresponding y-values.
